about: The US pack's packets, replacing the core ones with the same id.

packets.title: New patient intake
Annual update
Referral
Downtime kit
packets.about: For a system outage: registration, the routing slip, the visit note, the superbill for charges and the summary the patient takes home, all on paper to enter afterwards.

packets.title: Language help (notice of availability, interpreter request)
packets.about: For a patient who prefers another language: the Section 1557 notice of free language help, the interpreter request, and how they want to be contacted.

packets.title: Records from another office (records request and release)
packets.about: To get records from another provider: the request, with the signed release of information.

packets.title: Patient requests: blank forms to stock the front desk
packets.about: One of each request a patient may make under HIPAA and Section 1557: their records, a correction, a restriction, a list of disclosures, taking back an authorization, and a grievance. Print to stock; hand out the one asked for.

packets.title: Uninsured or self-pay (good faith estimate and sliding fee)
packets.about: For a patient with no insurance, or not using it: the good faith estimate the No Surprises Act requires, with the sliding fee application and notice.

packets.title: Notices to post in the office
packets.about: The notices a US health center posts where patients see them: nondiscrimination, free language help, the sliding fee discount, and the right to a good faith estimate.

packets.title: Medicare patient: other insurance questions
packets.about: The questions Medicare asks providers to use to find out whether another payer pays first. Ask at the first visit, then ask whether anything has changed.

packets.title: Yearly adult screen (anxiety, depression, substance use and food)
packets.about: Every adult, once a year: the short first stage of each screen. A positive answer opens its follow-up: the GAD-7 or PHQ-9 after the PHQ-4, TAPS-2 after TAPS-1, the six-item survey after the Hunger Vital Sign. A positive food screen counts in UDS Table 6A (line 40) once it is recorded as a coded problem.

packets.title: Preventive care questions (once, and when things change)
packets.about: The answers that decide which USPSTF screenings and preventive medicines are due: pack-years, cancers in close relatives, sexual health, where the patient was born and has lived, and pregnancy.

packets.title: After a positive food screen (six-item food security survey)
packets.about: For a positive Hunger Vital Sign: the USDA six-item survey says how severe the food insecurity is.

packets.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit (health risk assessment and screens)
packets.about: Before a Medicare Annual Wellness Visit: the health risk assessment, a depression screen, falls risk, a substance use screen, and the preventive care questions that set the screening schedule. Cognition is checked in the visit by direct observation.

packets.title: Care management enrollment (consent and medicine review)
packets.about: Before Medicare care management services: the consent, with each thing CMS says the patient must be told, and a medicine review.

packets.title: Vaccine visit (vaccine record and information statements)
packets.about: A paper record of each vaccine given, with the Vaccine Information Statement edition and date the law asks for. Print each statement from CDC at the time.

packets.title: Pregnancy and postpartum screen (depression, substance use, food, relationship safety)
packets.about: At a prenatal or postpartum visit: the PHQ-9 for perinatal depression, TAPS-1, the Hunger Vital Sign and HARK. Give HARK when the patient is alone.

packets.title: Who we serve: UDS questions and the sliding fee (short annual update)
packets.about: Housing status, agricultural work and veteran status, with household income for the sliding fee. Feeds UDS Tables 3A, 3B and 4 and the 330(g), (h) and (i) Grant Reports.

packets.title: Substance use treatment intake (42 CFR Part 2)
Title X family planning visit
packets.about: For a family planning visit in a Title X project: the notice of what patients can expect (privacy, minors, the statement a policyholder may get, charges by income), the income and household size Title X charges by, and the visit record whose coded answers the Title X Report reads for FPAR 2.0.
